title: Modules, packages, virtual environments and dependencies
summary: A module is a .py file; a package is a folder of modules, usually with __init__.py.

sections.definition: A module is a .py file; a package is a folder of modules (usually with __init__.py). A virtual environment isolates each project's interpreter and libraries. The current FastAPI documentation uses uv by default, with pyproject.toml and uv.lock.
sections.analogy: The virtual environment is each project's own pantry: you don't take ingredients from the common market or change your neighbor's recipe.
sections.problem: Without a virtual environment, two projects that need different versions of a library break each other, and what you installed into the system Python can break Mac tools.
sections.code:example:
# Terminal (recomendado: uv)
uv init tienda-api && cd tienda-api
uv add "fastapi[standard]"
uv run fastapi dev app/main.py

# Alternativa clásica con venv + pip
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install "fastapi[standard]"

# Estructura e imports
# app/
#   __init__.py
#   main.py
#   productos/
#     __init__.py
#     router.py
from app.productos.router import router as productos_router

if __name__ == "__main__":     # solo si ejecutas el archivo directamente
    print("modo script")
sections.bad:
sudo pip install fastapi
from utilidades import *

Global installation and a star import that fills the namespace without knowing what it brings in.
sections.good:
uv add "fastapi[standard]"
from app.utilidades import calcular_iva

Dependency recorded in pyproject.toml and locked in uv.lock; explicit import.
sections.bridge:typescript: pyproject.toml ≈ package.json; uv.lock ≈ package-lock.json; .venv ≈ node_modules, but it also contains the interpreter; PyPI ≈ npm registry; uv run ≈ npx/npm run. Key difference: Node finds node_modules on its own; Python uses whichever environment is active, or the one uv run activates for you.
sections.interview: Each .py file is a module and a folder of modules is a package. I isolate each project in a virtual environment so its dependencies don't clash with other projects or with the system. Today I use uv: it declares dependencies in pyproject.toml and pins exact versions in uv.lock, just like package.json and the lockfile in Node. The if name equals main block lets a module be both importable and executable.
sections.myths:
• Installing without activating the venv and then not finding the package.
  • Naming your file fastapi.py or json.py: it shadows the real library on import.
  • Circular imports between modules (A imports B and B imports A).
  • Committing the .venv folder to the repo.

items.q: Which file plays the role of package-lock.json with uv?
items.why: uv.lock pins the exact versions of the whole dependency tree.

items.q: When does the code inside if __name__ == "__main__": run?
options: When the file is run directly, not when it's imported
When it's imported for the first time
items.why: On import, __name__ is the module's name; when run directly it's "__main__".
